A static website: the page is `site/index.html`, its styles are in `site/css/`, its scripts in `site/js/` and its images in `site/assets/`.

- `npm start` serves the site on http://127.0.0.1:$PORT (the `PORT` variable is set).

content.text:
I couldn't find anything in the site that needs fixing, so I haven't changed any files. The visual test is still failing at both desktop and phone size.

**What differs:** I compared the current render with the approved screenshots. The layout matches exactly: sections, images, colours and spacing are all the same. Only the text is different. Most body text in the approved screenshots is about 1% wider. For example, the footer line is about 245px wide there and 242px now. The `h2` headings are the exception and match.

**What I ruled out:** The repo has a single commit, so there's no earlier version to diff against. The HTML and CSS look like a normal Bootstrap page. The only custom rule is `.bg-image-full`. `server.js` doesn't alter anything it serves. I tried three things in the browser to reproduce the approved text widths: turning kerning off, switching to Inter Display, and switching to Liberation Sans. None of them matched the screenshots.

**Likely cause:** The font stack resolves to Inter through `system-ui`, and several of the other named fonts in the stack also resolve to Inter on this machine. The approved screenshots were probably rendered with a slightly different font build or font setup. That would point to the machine's fonts rather than a CSS change. I haven't confirmed this.

**What I need from you:** What looked different to you? If you can tell me which part of the page looks wrong, I can look there. If the page looks right to you, the approved screenshots are probably stale, and I can regenerate them with `npx playwright test --update-snapshots`. I haven't done that, because it would make the test pass without fixing anything.

STATUS: NOT DONE
